work.permit: work permit from the Department of Labor and Employment

note: Read first on 2026-10-31 on the Lawphil Project (Arellano Law Foundation), which publishes the Acts' texts as enacted; the Official Gazette's site answered with a Cloudflare challenge. Majority: Republic Act No. 6809 (1989), amending the Family Code, art. 234: majority commences at eighteen, which emancipates (art. 236, not read: an emancipated person is qualified for all acts of civil life, save marriage consent under twenty-one). Work: Republic Act No. 9231 (2003), s. 2, amending s. 12 of RA 7610: children below fifteen may not be employed, save two exceptions; from fifteen to seventeen work is allowed outside hazardous work and within hours limits (no work from 10 pm to 6 am; not held). Exception 1, work in a family enterprise under the parents' sole responsibility, isn't held. Performers: exception 2: a child below fifteen may be employed in public entertainment or information through cinema, theatre, radio, television or other media where the participation is essential, on a contract the parents conclude, with the child's agreement where possible and the Department of Labor and Employment's approval; the employer must first secure a work permit from the Department (the 'Working Child Permit'). Below fifteen: at most twenty hours a week, none between 8 pm and 6 am (not held); a trust fund of 30% of earnings above P200,000 a year (not held). No lowest age. Service: Service is held null: no source saying no service is asked was reached today (the blocker file names the attempts); a reading only, not held: there is no conscription (the National Service Training Program, RA 9163, is a college course; not read). Read again 2026-11-03 in the Supreme Court E-Library (elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph), the Judiciary's own register of statutes, which gives the same words; the Lawphil copies first read are no longer cited.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 6809, An Act Lowering the Age of Majority from Twenty-One to Eighteen Years (Supreme Court E-Library)
sources.said: ART. 234. Emancipation takes place by the attainment of majority. Unless otherwise provided, majority commences at the age of eighteen years.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 9231, December 19, 2003 (Supreme Court E-Library)
sources.said: "SEC. 12. Employment of Children. - Children below fifteen (15) years of age shall not be employed except: ... "2 Where a child's employment or participation in public entertainment or information through cinema, theater, radio, television or other forms of media is essential: Provided, That the employment contract is concluded by the child's parents or legal guardian, with the express agreement of the child concerned, if possible, and the approval of the Department of Labor and Employment ... "In the above-exceptional cases where any such child may be employed, the employer shall first secure, before engaging such child, a work permit from the Department of Labor and Employment
